newsitem.title: UK: Tanker broke up off Japan due to corrosion - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Tanker broke up off Japan due to corrosion - Jiji.

text.p: Heavy corrosion has been cited as the reason for the loss of a Russian tanker off the coast of Japan in January, according to the Jiji Press agency.

Jiji Press reported Monday that a Japanese Transport Ministry investigation panel has found that the 20,471dwt Nakhodka broke up off Shimane Prefecture because its frame was unable to withstand the pounding of waves of between eight and 15 metres.
According to sources at the Ministry, tests have shown that the 27 year old ship's deck and hull were so corroded they were 20 percent to 30 percent thinner than designed.
Investigators were also said to have discovered oil was loaded in tanks too close to the bow which accelerated buckling of the deck section.
The full findings are expected to be presented at a meeting between the Japanese ministry and the Russian government in Moscow on July 14. - Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5107.
